method: Instruction listings decoded directly from the PE bytes of the identified executable through its section table, with the executable size and SHA-256 verified first. Every cited instruction address, operand, name literal, holder vftable cell, type descriptor name, RTTI name and call target was compared with those listings. Callers were enumerated by scanning the .text section for rel32 call and jmp instructions, so virtual and indirect callers are not covered. Addresses are absolute virtual addresses. No decompiled body is a tracked evidence dependency.
scope: Static Lua call contracts of ten natives that the earlier contracts do not record: the chara scheduler natives _runCharaScheduler, _waitForCharaSchedulerFinished and _setGroundOn, the timed yield _wait, the item and package accessors _getItem, _getEquippingItem, _getItemPackageCapacity, _getCatalogID and _getNameIndex, and the log output _printLog. Each row gives the registration site, receiver type check, declared argument and return lists, reads, client state effects, failure behavior and yield behavior. The framework records the thread yield and resume machinery that _wait and _waitForCharaSchedulerFinished share, the identity lookup that the scheduler natives use, and the item package lookup that the item natives share. Client-side contracts do not establish scheduler content, item data, Lua wrapper logic or server behavior.
evidenceTier: MIXED, see tierVocabulary and the tier of each fact

tierVocabulary.STATIC: Read directly from instructions or data at the cited addresses.
tierVocabulary.INFERRED: A name or role assigned from the surrounding instructions. The bytes do not state it.

framework.reference: manifests/spreadsheet_native_call_contract.json framework, manifests/widget_native_call_contract.json framework and manifests/talk_native_call_contract.json framework: registration, the 0x00CC9D60 type registry, argument marshalling through 0x00D19A20, the holder receiver adapter, the invalid-parameter route and the return pushers.

registration.note: Each switchboard is slot 2 of its class vftable and has the shape recorded for SpreadSheet: it tests the byte at its argument +0x0E before each step and calls one registrar per step with one rel32 caller. The order of a native is its position among the registrar calls of its switchboard, which are spaced 0x15 bytes apart from the first call to the last cited one.

framework.listOrder: Every registrar builds the return list first and the argument list second, zeroes EDI, loads the callback into ESI, calls a per-class wrapper and installs the functor through 0x00CCCAD0 under the name built by 0x00447260. The adjustment is 0 in every row.
framework.receiverAdapter: Every holder invoke routine passes the receiver LuaControl (source type descriptor 0x01270B4C) and its own target type descriptor to 0x009DA6CC. A null cast returns false without calling the callback and the 0x00D19B70 failure path reports it as recorded in the talk contract framework. A successful cast adds the adjustment stored at holder +0x0C and calls the member function pointer at holder +0x08 with ExecuteParameters on the stack. The holder RTTI names carry the member function qualifier: BEX for const and AEX for non-const.

worldObject.chain: R is the address that 0x00CC7510 returns for ExecuteParameters +0x04. The callbacks read X = [R], Y = [X +0x04], W = [Y] and V = [W]. 0x0075C420 and its siblings, 0x0075D450 and 0x0075D4C0 take the ECX that holds W or the address of a local that holds W and load V from it. The sheet manager chain of the SpreadSheet contracts reaches the same V through 0x0075F5A0.

fields.+0x04AC: Identity registry. 0x004D9970 adds 0x4AC to V and calls 0x004DE190.

worldObject.tier: STATIC for the offsets and the chain, INFERRED for the roles. The class of V was not identified.

routines.0x004DE190: Returns 0 for the identity 0xC0000000. Otherwise finds the identity in the tree at registry +0x38 through 0x0071D420 and returns the dword at node +0x10, or 0 when the find reaches the head.
routines.0x0075C420: Takes a pointer to an identity and an int. Resolves the identity through 0x004D9970 and calls 0x0058CAF0 on the result with the int. No null test follows the lookup.
routines.0x0075C400: Takes an output pair, a pointer to an identity and an int. Resolves the identity and stores the result at pair +0x00 and the int at pair +0x04.
routines.0x0075C3E0: Takes a pointer to an identity and a bool. Resolves the identity and calls 0x00586750 on the result with the bool. No null test follows the lookup.

identityLookup.tier: STATIC for the routines, INFERRED for the registry role.

threadYield.yieldRequest: 0x00CD2860 is called with ECX = the Lua thread at ExecuteParameters +0x08 and one stack argument, a resume checker pointer. It calls 0x00CCD390 on the dword at thread +0x04 with the checker and a zero flag byte. 0x00CCD390 is LuaThreadImpl::YieldLua by its diagnostic literal at 0x0110E44C. With the flag byte zero it compares the byte at +0x138 of its receiver with the byte at 0x01377FBA and on a mismatch formats the literal with line 0x27F and calls 0x00CF3360 and 0x00CF38A0. It then calls 0x00CF1980 on the dword at +0x1C0 of the object at receiver +0x0C, stores the checker at receiver +0xE8 after calling slot 0 with argument 1 on a different nonnull previous checker, and calls 0x00CF0940.
threadYield.yieldGuard: The byte at +0x138 of the LuaThreadImpl is the yield state. YieldLua accepts the state equal to the byte at 0x01377FBA, which is 0 in the zero fill. 0x00CD27B0 sets the state to the byte at 0x0130D425 (2) when it equals the allowed byte. 0x00CD2830 resets the state to the allowed byte unless it equals the byte at 0x0130D424 (1), in which case it calls 0x00CD63F0. The callback of _restrictYieldFunction at 0x006DBD20 reaches them through 0x0078BFC0. The state names are INFERRED.
threadYield.yieldTest: 0x00CCD380 returns whether the dword at +0xE8 of its receiver is nonzero.
threadYield.functorExecutor: 0x00D19B70 is Component::Lua::GameEngine::Functor::Execute by its diagnostic literal at 0x0110F57C. It calls the holder invoke slot at 0x00D19D3B and after the invoke tests 0x00CCD380 at 0x00D19DD7. A set test takes the branch at 0x00D19DE4 that calls a virtual slot +0x04 of the object at +0x218 of its second argument. That argument is INFERRED to be the engine object because it also supplies the member at +0x1C0 that YieldLua reads from the engine at thread implementation +0x0C. A clear test takes the branch at 0x00D19F0A.
threadYield.checkerPoll: 0x00CCD4A0 reads the checker at thread +0xE8. A null checker stores the dword at 0x0130CED0 in the result cell. Otherwise it calls checker slot 1 with the result cell.
threadYield.updateLoop: 0x00CF1B50 is called from 0x00CC98B5. For each thread it reaches it calls 0x00CCD4A0 at 0x00CF1CD7. A result equal to the dword at 0x0130CECC leaves the thread parked at 0x00CF1CE8. Any other result resumes the thread through 0x00CCF290, or through 0x00CCE1C0 when the result equals the dword at 0x0130CED0. The loop is also bounded by a timeGetTime budget from the word at +0x3C of its receiver.

resultCells.0x01377ECC: Value 0. Stored by checkers that are done. No instruction in .text stores to it with an absolute operand.
resultCells.0x0130CECC: Value 1 in the file image. Stored by checkers that still wait.
resultCells.0x0130CED0: Value 2 in the file image. Stored by 0x00CCD4A0 for a thread without a checker.
resultCells.tier: STATIC for the values and the compares, INFERRED for the done, waiting and no checker readings. The cell at 0x01377ECC lies beyond the raw data of .data, so the value 0 is the loader zero fill.

itemPackages.packageManager: 0x006F51A0 returns the dword at owner +0xD8. A null dword allocates 0x78 bytes through 0x009D1B35, constructs the manager with 0x006F5100 and stores it at owner +0xD8. The owner is the CharaBase for the Chara natives and the dword at ItemBase +0x64 for the ItemBase natives.
itemPackages.oneBased: 0x0078BC90 and 0x0078BCD0 return their argument minus 1. The item natives pass the package and slot arguments through them, so Lua uses 1-based values. 0x0078BCA0, 0x0078BCE0 and the range tests at 0x0078BCB0 and 0x0078BCF0 are the inverse adapters.
itemPackages.packageFind: 0x006E5BA0 is a lower-bound find on the tree at manager +0x08 keyed by a dword. It returns the dword at node +0x10 or 0 when the key is absent.
itemPackages.slotFind: 0x006EE3E0 takes a pointer to a package key dword and a slot. It finds the package in the tree at manager +0x08, indexes the vector at package record +0x10 through 0x0052F7F0 and reads the slot descriptor pointer. A null descriptor returns 0. A descriptor with a nonzero dword at +0x08 returns that dword. A descriptor with a zero dword at +0x08 and neither dword +0x0C nor dword +0x10 equal to -1 repeats the lookup with the package key at +0x0C and the slot at +0x10. Any other descriptor returns 0. 0x006EE480 is the same routine on the tree at manager +0x14.
itemPackages.slotRange: 0x0052F7F0 calls 0x005CF390 when the index is not below the vector size, an unsigned compare, so index -1 from a Lua slot of 0 also throws. 0x005CF390 builds the message literal invalid vector<T> subscript at 0x00F9D618.
itemPackages.itemControl: 0x006E2770 builds a control, casts it to ItemBase with the type descriptor 0x012C0864 at 0x006E28F4 and stores the dword at +0x64, the dword at +0x68, the dword at +0x6C and a byte at +0x70. Those are the four ItemBase fields that 0x00701820 and 0x00701BF0 read. A stack ItemBase built by 0x006DD450 with vftable 0x00FD5484 and destroyed by 0x006DD4D0 surrounds the call. The callers push the returned control through 0x00748B30.
itemPackages.tier: STATIC for the routines and offsets, INFERRED for every role.

argumentReaders.0x005819A0: Reads cell tag 0, the int. A mismatched tag reaches 0x00CCA730.
argumentReaders.0x0071BC90: Reads cell tag 4, a LuaControl*, casts it to CharaBase with 0x009DA6CC and the type descriptor 0x012709A4 and on a failed non-null cast reports through 0x00CCA730.

returnPushers.0x00748920: Nil, built as a tag 6 cell

framework.invalidParameterRoute: A failed cell vector size test calls 0x009D22B4. The target cursor contract records that routine as the invalid-parameter route that ends in TerminateProcess.
framework.scriptBinding: Each row's scriptBinding names the class and script that xivl-client-scripts:lua/napi_index.json lists for the native. The wrapper methods in the _u scripts were not read.

arguments.note: Scheduler identifier. The callback passes it unchanged to the chara scheduler queue entry.

rows.behavior: Reads one int and resolves the receiver identity to the Chara object through the identity registry. It builds a scheduler request for the int and appends it to the queue container at Chara +0xA80. It pushes no value and requests no yield, so the Lua call returns as soon as the request is queued. A receiver identity that is not in the registry reaches the Chara call with a null this.

facts.claim: The argument is read at cell 0 through 0x005819A0 after a cell vector size test that calls 0x009D22B4 on failure.
The callback never touches the return container at ExecuteParameters +0x1C and never calls the yield request 0x00CD2860. It ends with ret 4 after one call.

The callback reaches the world object through 0x00CC7510 on ExecuteParameters +0x04 and calls 0x0075C420 with the address of a local that holds the receiver identity from ExecuteParameters +0x0C and the int.

0x0075C420 resolves the identity through 0x004D9970 and 0x004DE190 and calls 0x0058CAF0 on the result with the int. The lookup returns 0 for the identity 0xC0000000 and for an identity that is not in the tree at registry +0x38. No null test follows it.
0x0058CAF0 pushes a zero, reads the dword at this +0x88 through 0x004D6750 and calls 0x0058C690 with the int, that dword and the zero. 0x004D6750 reads this +0x88 without a null test.

0x0058C690 zero fills a 0x38 byte record through 0x009D2110, stores the three arguments and the constants 1 and 1 in it, classifies the int through 0x00585800 with the default 5, builds the queue entry through 0x00587370 and appends it through 0x005901D0 to the container at this +0xA80.

0x00585800 returns a category from its first argument, 5 here, or from 7 to 0x11. It chooses by comparing fields that 0x00798370 and 0x007982D0 split out of the identifier, and it returns the first argument when no case matches.

The int is a chara scheduler identifier and the container at Chara +0xA80 is the queue that runs it. The names come from the native name and the _waitForCharaSchedulerFinished poll, which looks the same identifier up in per-category queues of the same Chara.
What consumes the queue at Chara +0xA80, how an entry runs, and the run-time behavior of a null Chara after the lookup. The Lua wrapper in chara/charabaseclass_u was not read.

corpusCallSites.sitesNote: Per-line sites are omitted for size. Rebuild them from the callsites list of this native in xivl-client-scripts:lua/napi_index.json.

arguments.note: Wait time in seconds. The body multiplies it by 1000.0 and truncates it to a signed 64 bit millisecond duration.

rows.behavior: Reads one float and builds a WaitResumeChecker that holds the duration in milliseconds and the timeGetTime value at construction. It requests a yield of the calling Lua thread with that checker through 0x00CD2860 and returns at once. The checker poll reports done when the elapsed milliseconds reach the duration. The receiver is cast to ActorBase and otherwise unused.

facts.claim: The callback constructs an empty adapter with 0x0078B8C0, calls the body 0x0078BED0 with ExecuteParameters and destroys the adapter with 0x0078B8D0. It does not read the receiver.
The argument is read at cell 0 through 0x0071BAC0 after a cell vector size test that calls 0x009D22B4 on failure.
The duration is the float converted to a double, multiplied by the double 1000.0 at 0x00F91C48, truncated by cvttsd2si and sign extended to 64 bits. A negative argument gives a negative 64 bit value.

A 0x28 byte object is allocated through 0x009D1B35 and constructed by 0x0078B850 with the low and high duration dwords stored at +0x08 and +0x0C. The constructor sets the vftable 0x00FD4F5C, then 0x00FE0548, and runs 0x00D353F0 on +0x10. A failed allocation passes a null checker.

0x00D353F0 stores the result of the import WINMM.dll timeGetTime, IAT cell 0x00F3E55C, at +0x08 of its receiver and zero at +0x0C. For the checker these are the dwords at +0x18 and +0x1C. It also stores the pair that 0x004CFA50 returns at receiver +0x10 and +0x14.

The vftable 0x00FE0548 has the RTTI name .?AVWaitResumeChecker@?A0x1eef0f3d@@ with slot 0 0x0078D980, slot 1 0x0078D940 and slot 2 0x00A72A20. Its base vftable 0x00FD4F5C is .?AVResumeCheckerInterface@GameEngine@Lua@Component@@.
The yield request loads ECX from ExecuteParameters +0x08 and calls 0x00CD2860 with the checker pointer. The callback returns after the call.

The poll in slot 1 calls timeGetTime, subtracts the dwords at +0x18 and +0x1C as a 64 bit value and compares the result with the duration at +0x08 and +0x0C, high dword first, with unsigned compares. An elapsed value that is not below the duration stores the dword at 0x01377ECC in the result cell. A smaller value stores the dword at 0x0130CECC.

The cell values read as done for 0x01377ECC (0) and still waiting for 0x0130CECC (1), because the update loop leaves the thread parked on 0x0130CECC and resumes it on every other result. A negative argument has a high dword of 0xFFFFFFFF, which the unsigned high compare treats as greater than a normal elapsed value, so the poll keeps reporting waiting. A zero argument is done at the first poll, which runs after the native has returned.

Whether the per-thread timer scheduler that docs/client-architecture.md names (0x00CEF510 and 0x00CCEAC0) also touches a _wait thread, the body of 0x00A72A20, and the effect of a missing or non-float argument beyond the marshalling framework.

arguments.note: Scheduler identifier, the value that _runCharaScheduler takes.

rows.behavior: Reads one int, resolves the receiver identity to the Chara object and builds a WaitForCharaSchedulerFinishedResumeChecker that holds the Chara pointer and the int. It requests a yield of the calling Lua thread with that checker and returns at once. The checker poll reports waiting while the Chara still holds a queue entry for the identifier and done afterwards.

facts.claim: The argument is read at cell 0 through 0x005819A0 after a cell vector size test that calls 0x009D22B4 on failure.
0x0075C400 resolves the receiver identity from ExecuteParameters +0x0C through the identity registry and stores the Chara pointer and the int in a local pair. No null test follows the lookup.

A 0x0C byte object is allocated through 0x009D1B35 and constructed by 0x006DC0E0 from the pair. The constructor sets the vftable 0x00FD50FC and stores the Chara pointer at +0x04 and the int at +0x08. The checker stores the pointer, not the identity.

The vftable 0x00FD50FC has the RTTI name .?AVWaitForCharaSchedulerFinishedResumeChecker@?1??_waitForCharaSchedulerFinished@CharaBase@Control@Client@Script@Lua@Application@@QBEXABVExecuteParameters@GameEngine@6Component@@@Z@. Slot 0 is 0x007187D0, slot 1 0x006DC150 and slot 2 0x006DC180.
The yield request loads ECX from ExecuteParameters +0x08 and calls 0x00CD2860 with the checker pointer. The callback returns after the call.

The poll in slot 1 calls 0x00758CE0 on the pair, which calls 0x0058AB60 on the Chara with the int. A result of 1 stores the dword at 0x0130CECC in the result cell. Any other result stores the dword at 0x01377ECC.

0x0058AB60 maps the int to a category with 0x00585800 and the default 5, calls 0x00589F60 with the category and the int and returns whether the result is nonzero. 0x00589F60 returns 0 for a category outside 1 to 0x19. Otherwise it walks the ring of entry pointers at Chara +0x878 + category * 0x14 and returns 1 when an entry has a dword at +0x10 equal to the int.

The ring at Chara +0x878 + category * 0x14 is the set of running scheduler entries per category and the dword at entry +0x10 is the identifier. The same 0x00585800 category rule files the request that _runCharaScheduler queues, so the wait ends when the identifier has left its category. The roles come from the native names.
Whether the entry ring at +0x878 is fed from the queue at +0xA80, what happens to a checker whose Chara was freed while the thread waits, and the destructor bodies at slots 0 and 2.

returns.note: The dword at +0x24 of the item record.

rows.behavior: Reads the owner, package key, slot and variant byte from the ItemBase control, finds the item record through the package manager of the owner and pushes the dword at record +0x24 as an int. It takes no argument and requests no yield. A lookup that returns 0 is not tested.

facts.claim: The callback loads the byte at +0x70, the dword at +0x6C and the address +0x68 of the ItemBase control and the owner dword at +0x64 into registers.

It calls 0x006F51A0 on the owner dword, which returns the package manager. A variant byte equal to 1 selects 0x006EE480 and any other value selects 0x006EE3E0. Both take the address of the key at +0x68 and the slot dword from +0x6C.

The result is dereferenced at +0x24 with no null test. A lookup that returns 0 reads the address 0x00000024. The dword is pushed as an int through 0x00584F70 with the return container from ExecuteParameters +0x1C.

The dword at +0x24 is the catalog identifier of the item, from the native name. The four ItemBase fields are the reference that 0x006E2770 stores when it builds the control, so the call re-reads the package on every call.
Which structure holds the record and what the variant byte at +0x70 selects. The tree at manager +0x14 that 0x006EE480 reads was not identified.

arguments.note: Package number. The helper subtracts 1 through 0x0078BC90.
Slot number. The helper subtracts 1 through 0x0078BCD0.

returns.note: An ItemBase control, or nil when no record is found.

rows.behavior: Reads two ints, converts them from 1-based to 0-based, finds the item slot in the package manager of the receiver and pushes an ItemBase control that references it. A lookup that returns 0 pushes nil. The sibling _getExtendedTemporaryItem calls the same helper 0x00702400 with flag 1.

arguments.note: Chara to query. The reader casts it to CharaBase.

facts.claim: The argument list builder 0x0072C0E0 fills three entries. Entry 0 is registry entry 4 and entries 1 and 2 come from 0x007270B0, which returns registry entry 0 for those indexes. The callback reads cell 0 through 0x0071BC90, cell 1 and cell 2 through 0x005819A0.

The lookup repeats the 0x006F51A0, 0x006E5BA0 and 0x006EE3E0 sequence of the CharaBase registration on the Chara argument with both numbers decremented, pushes Nil for a 0 result and otherwise builds the control with 0x006E2770 and the flag 0.
The callback builds a stack ItemBase with 0x006DD450, calls the helper 0x00702400 with ExecuteParameters, the receiver and the flag 0, and destroys the stack object with 0x006DD4D0.
The helper reads cell 0 and cell 1 as ints through 0x005819A0, each after a cell vector size test that calls 0x009D22B4 on failure, and subtracts 1 from each through 0x0078BC90 and 0x0078BCD0.

It calls 0x006F51A0 on the receiver for the package manager and 0x006E5BA0 with the package key. The result of 0x006E5BA0 is not tested. It then calls 0x006EE3E0 with the address of the package key and the slot.
A result of 0 pushes Nil through 0x00748920 with the return container from ExecuteParameters +0x1C.
A nonzero record is passed to 0x006E2770 with the engine handle and the flag. The control it returns is pushed through 0x00748B30.

A slot at or beyond the end of the package slot vector reaches 0x0052F7F0 and then 0x005CF390, which builds the message invalid vector<T> subscript. A Lua slot of 0 becomes index -1, and the unsigned compare at 0x0052F80D..0x0052F811 also throws. A package key that is absent from the tree returns 0 and pushes Nil.

The first argument selects an item package of the Chara and the second a slot in it, with 1-based numbering from Lua. A slot descriptor can redirect to another package and slot, so the returned control can name a different package than the one asked for.
The meaning of the flag in 0x006E2770, the body of that routine up to the control it returns, and the package numbers that scripts use. The Lua wrapper in chara/charabaseclass_u was not read.

rows.behavior: Reads one Utf8String and hands it to the log sink of the world object with the kind 0x20 and an empty prefix string. It pushes no value and requests no yield. A second registration on the Debug class reads the same argument and uses the kind 0x1F with the prefix <debug>.

facts.claim: The callback builds a Utf8String from the literal <debug> at 0x00FD46D4 through 0x00447260 and calls 0x0075D4C0 with the engine handle, the kind 0x1F, that string, the text and a zero flag.
The argument is read at cell 0 through 0x0071CE70 after a cell vector size test that calls 0x009D22B4 on failure.

The callback reaches the world object through 0x00CC7510 and 0x0075D450 and calls 0x0075D4C0 with the engine handle, the kind 0x20, the static object at 0x01266B10, the text and a zero flag. The object at 0x01266B10 holds a text pointer that addresses a zero byte, so the prefix is empty.

0x0075D4C0 calls 0x004D6D90 on the world object with the kind, prefix, text and flag. 0x004D6D90 does nothing when the dword at world object +0x660 is null. A zero flag calls 0x004CE760 on that sink with the kind, the prefix and the text. A nonzero flag formats the prefix through 0x0044AB90 first.
The sink at world object +0x660 is the client log and chat output path and the kind selects the channel. The roles come from the native name and the call shape.
The body of 0x004CE760, the meaning of the kinds 0x1F and 0x20, and the consumers of the sink.

arguments.note: Equipment slot number. The helper subtracts 1 through 0x0078BCD0.

returns.note: An ItemBase control, or nil when the package or the slot has no record.

rows.behavior: Reads one int, converts it from 1-based to 0-based and looks it up as the slot of the package whose key is the dword at 0x00FE050C. A missing package or an empty slot pushes nil. Otherwise it pushes an ItemBase control that references the slot, built by the same routine as _getItem.

facts.claim: The callback builds a stack ItemBase with 0x006DD450, calls the helper 0x00702510 with ExecuteParameters, the receiver and the flag 0, and destroys the stack object with 0x006DD4D0.
The helper reads cell 0 as an int through 0x005819A0 after a cell vector size test that calls 0x009D22B4 on failure and subtracts 1 through 0x0078BCD0.
The package key is the dword 0x000000FE at 0x00FE050C. 0x006E5BA0 on the package manager of the receiver with that key returns 0 for a missing package, which pushes Nil.
0x006EE3E0 with the same key and the slot returns 0 for an empty slot, which pushes Nil. A nonzero record goes through 0x006E2770 with flag 0 and is pushed through 0x00748B30.
A slot at or beyond the end of the package slot vector, or a Lua slot of 0 (index -1, unsigned compare), reaches the invalid vector<T> subscript throw through 0x0052F7F0, as for _getItem.
The key 0xFE names the equipment package. The two following dwords at 0x00FE0510 and 0x00FE0514 hold 0xFD and 0xFC. The role comes from the native name and the use of a constant key.
Which equipment slot numbers scripts pass and the contents of the 0xFE package. The sibling _getExtendedTemporaryEquippingItem was not traced.

arguments.note: Package number. The helper subtracts 1 through 0x0078BC90.

returns.note: The dword at +0x08 of the package record, or 0 when the package is absent.

rows.behavior: Reads one int, converts it from 1-based to 0-based and finds the package record in the package manager of the receiver. It pushes the dword at record +0x08 as an int, or 0 when no record exists. It requests no yield.

facts.claim: The callback builds a stack ItemBase with 0x006DD450, calls the helper 0x00702740 with ExecuteParameters and the receiver, and destroys the stack object with 0x006DD4D0.
The helper reads cell 0 as an int through 0x005819A0 after a cell vector size test that calls 0x009D22B4 on failure and subtracts 1 through 0x0078BC90.
It calls 0x006F51A0 on the receiver and 0x006E5BA0 with the address of the package key. A result of 0 stores 0 and pushes it as an int through 0x00584F70.
A nonzero record pushes the dword at record +0x08 as an int through 0x00584F70 with the return container from ExecuteParameters +0x1C.
The dword at record +0x08 is the slot capacity of the package, from the native name. The package vector at record +0x10 that 0x006EE3E0 indexes is the slot storage.
How the record at +0x08 is written and whether a scripted package number outside the shipped numbering returns 0.

arguments.note: Ground state flag. The callback reduces it to a byte.

rows.behavior: Reads one bool, resolves the receiver identity to the Chara object and posts a scene packet of type 0x27 with a four byte payload that holds 0 or 1. It then clears the byte at receiver +0xE1. It pushes no value and requests no yield.

facts.claim: The argument is read at cell 0 through 0x0071BA00 after a cell vector size test that calls 0x009D22B4 on failure. The callback stores the byte in a local.

The callback calls 0x0075C3E0 with the address of a local that holds the receiver identity from ExecuteParameters +0x0C and the byte. 0x0075C3E0 resolves the identity through 0x004D9970 and calls 0x00586750 on the result. No null test follows the lookup.
0x00586750 turns the bool into the dword 0 or 1 and calls 0x004D7980 with the record number 0x12, the address of the dword and the size 4.
